authoredFrom: The pinned grammar's own node extents for THIS file, read off `wasm/tree-sitter-erlang.wasm` before the analyzer was run on it — not off analyzer output. ER-D26: Erlang has one function per (name, arity), so `pick/1` is ONE symbol whose range spans every `;`-separated clause and ends on the grammar's `fun_decl`. Measured for this file: fun_decl [1038,1058) and [1059,1078) against function_clause [1038,1057) and [1059,1077) — the two node types differ by exactly the clause-terminating `.`, and the second clause's fun_decl is the one that ends the function, so the merged end is 1078 and never 1077. `nodeToRange` publishes tree-sitter's EXCLUSIVE end as `endColumn: node.endPosition.column + 1`, which is why 1078 reads as endColumn 10 on line 21. The three shapes are: two clauses, two clauses whose last clause ends a line it does not start, and three clauses (so a range that stopped at the second clause would be visibly short rather than one character short).

expectSymbols.name: pick
expectSymbols.note:
ER-D44 merge path. Spans fun_decl [1038,1058) AND [1059,1078). The end is the SECOND clause's fun_decl (1078), not its function_clause (1077) and not the first clause's fun_decl (1058). Taking the clause ends the symbol one character early, so `source.slice(startIndex, endIndex)` — the text a consumer reads back — loses the closing `.` of `pick(X) ->
    {X}.`

expectSymbols.name: head
expectSymbols.note: ER-D44 merge path, with a clause head that is a PATTERN (`head([H|_])`). fun_decl [1218,1241) and [1242,1267) against function_clause [1218,1240) and [1242,1266): the merged end is 1267. The second clause ends on line 28 at column 14 (exclusive 15), so a range that ended on the FIRST clause's line would be caught here and not only by the column.

expectSymbols.name: wide
expectSymbols.note: ER-D26 + ER-D44 together: three clauses of one (name, arity) are ONE symbol, so the range must reach the THIRD clause's fun_decl [1406,1431). fun_decl extents are [1360,1382) [1383,1405) [1406,1431); a range stopping at the second clause would be 1405, twenty-six characters and two lines short, which is a visibly different defect from the one-character one.

expectSymbolCount.name: pick
expectSymbolCount.note: ER-D26: the two clauses merge into ONE symbol, so a reader asking for `pick` finds one function, not two.

expectSymbolCount.name: wide
expectSymbolCount.note: three clauses, one symbol — the case that separates 'merged' from 'the first clause won'.
